cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I spent my Saturday fixing your fence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you to next door. They've got six panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them three took my whole Saturday before you make me sound available for Sunday.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A5 directs the recommendation wording, but A3 question restriction does not act as a specific permission response.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 three-panel minimization causes A3 detailed work list; B4 larger job offer causes A5 insistence on time acknowledgment.

relationship.evidence: B2 underestimates scale and B4 offers what may be a compliment, plausibly misunderstanding what recognition A seeks.

heightening.evidence: B4 six-panel opportunity makes A5 explain why praise must include the full Saturday rather than imply availability.

specificity.evidence: A1 Saturday fence work and A3 counts make the practical contribution concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 Saturday-versus-Sunday consequence is earned by B4 proposed follow-on job, with a clumsy A3 preface.
